name: NGC 1281 (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 1281, a compact elliptical galaxy in the Perseus Cluster, seen by Hubble.
label: ngc1281-hubble
story: A small, dense elliptical galaxy in the Perseus Cluster, a nearby echo of the compact galaxies of the early universe. Its stars move as if wrapped in a massive halo of dark matter.

claims.text: NGC 1281 is a compact early-type galaxy in the Perseus Cluster with E5 (elliptical) classification
NGC 1281 is dark matter dominated, with a massive dark halo
NGC 1281 is a compact elliptical galaxy imaged by Hubble program GO-13050
Nearby compact elliptical galaxies are dense, are outliers today, and resemble the compact, massive, quiescent galaxies of the early universe (local analogues)
Hubble program 13050 'The Most Massive Black Holes in Small Galaxies' imaged NGC1281 to hunt for overmassive black holes in compact early-type galaxies
